free_tier.stated: 2 TB €129.95 once · 6 TB €279.95 once (official site). StackSocial carries 2/6/12/20 TB SKUs at $59.95 / $139.95 / — / $349.95.

egress.terms: "Unlimited bandwidth" stated on both the official pricing page and the StackSocial listing. No counter, no fair-use figure published.

interface_detail: WebDAV (Premium only), CLI with a local WebDAV server, desktop client, web app
tooling: rclone as a WebDAV remote against either the CLI's local WebDAV server (`scramble-cli webdav`) or the hosted endpoint. Documented by the vendor.
chaining: composition with the pool is unestablished

limits.value: review reads the same listing as 7 GB/day

limits_note: The deal-killer for bulk work, quoted from the StackSocial listing: "Maximum File Size: 5GB per file" and "Daily Upload Limit: 70GB per day". A third-party review reads the same listing as 7 GB/day. Either number makes 20 TB an ~285-2,850 day upload. Also: "WebDAV requires a Premium account" and the free tier is WebDAV-less.
reliability_note: German provider, ISO 27001 infrastructure, E2E encrypted. Real product, but the lifetime SKUs are retail-consumer-shaped: per-file and per-day write caps, desktop client described as beta in reviews.

evidence.proved: and https://docs.scramble.cloud/cli/ — rclone-over-WebDAV instructions (opened via search snippets)

price_per_tb_month: One-time, so amortise: 6 TB at €279.95 = €46.66/TB once; over 5 years that is €0.78/TB/mo, over 3 years €1.30/TB/mo. 20 TB SKU at $349.95 = $17.50/TB once = $0.29/TB/mo over 5 years. at 5 TB: the 6 TB SKU. at 20 TB: the 20 TB SKU.
